dedupe_keys.name: savannah georgia cost of a hurricane evacuation for a coastal hospital

description: This case study estimates what it costs a coastal hospital to evacuate ahead of a hurricane. The authors, from Memorial Health University Medical Center in Savannah, Georgia and the University of Georgia, used the hospital's own financial data, including average inpatient and outpatient revenues, personnel wages and patient transport costs, and published the analysis in an open-access journal article. Coverage is one hospital. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence; the financial data are summarised in the article only. Caveats: the estimate is for one hospital and one evacuation scenario, and it excludes the cost of returning patients and of storm damage, which the authors flag as further costs. The study found that the hospital would spend about 9.5 million dollars on evacuation and lost revenue even before tropical storm force winds arrive, with revenue losses continuing until regular operations resume after landfall; forward planning, infrastructure upgrades and fast resumption of services can reduce the burden. Simulation uses: cost parameters for evacuate or shelter-in-place decisions in hospital resilience and emergency response models. Related records: the Hurricane Sandy New York City hospital evacuations (case_study-hurricane-sandy-nyc-hospital-evacuations) and the Hurricane Irene North Shore-LIJ evacuation (case_study-hurricane-irene-nslij-hospital-evacuation) document other hospital evacuations.
